d: The General Accountant is responsible for the accurate and timely recording of the organization's day-to-day financial transactions and for maintaining complete and reliable general ledger accounts and accounting records. The role ensures that journal entries, accruals, payments, and adjusting entries are properly prepared and supported, providing management with dependable financial information for reporting and decision-making. The position maintains accounts payable and accounts receivable records, supports inventory reconciliations and stock adjustments where applicable, and investigates discrepancies between physical counts and accounting records. In doing so, the General Accountant safeguards the integrity of the company's financial records and ensures compliance with IFRS, applicable tax regulations, company financial policies, and internal control procedures.
q: Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. Professional certifications such as SOCPA, CMA, or CPA are an advantage.
2–5 years of relevant accounting experience, preferably within a retail, restaurant, or multi-unit operating environment. Hands-on experience with an ERP system (e.g., SAP or Oracle) is required.
Good knowledge of accounting principles and financial reporting.
Familiarity with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
Familiarity with applicable tax regulations (e.g., ZATCA/VAT).
Understanding of general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and month-end closing processes.
Knowledge of inventory reconciliation and stock adjustment procedures.
Understanding of company financial policies and internal control procedures.
Experience working with ERP systems for transaction processing and reporting.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Accuracy and high attention to detail.
Time management and prioritization, with the ability to meet deadlines.
Communication and teamwork skills in both Arabic and English.
r: Accurate, complete, and timely recording of daily financial transactions in the accounting (ERP) system, supported by proper documentation.
Accurate and up-to-date general ledger accounts and accounting records, with balances reconciled and supported at each period-end.
Correct preparation of journal entries, accruals, payments, and adjusting entries in line with accounting principles and the month-end close timetable.
Accurate and current AP and AR records, with supplier and customer balances reconciled and outstanding items followed up.
Support for inventory reconciliations and stock adjustments, where applicable, ensuring book records agree with physical counts.
Timely investigation and resolution of differences between physical counts and accounting records, with root causes documented and corrective entries posted.
Full adherence to IFRS, applicable tax regulations, company financial policies, and internal control procedures, with no material audit findings.
Accurate and timely provision of accounting data and schedules to support month-end close, financial reporting, and audit requirements.
